title: Outer-Boundary Assisted Segmentation and Quantification of Trabecular Bones by an Imagej Plugin
protocol: Install ImageJ software.
Download the Windows version of ImageJ (version 1.51p) bundled with 64-bit Java from https://imagej.nih.gov/ij/.
Extract the downloaded software into a folder, which will be subsequently referred to as the "ImageJ Directory".
Request trabecular analysis plugins from http://www.bomomics.com.
Unzip the contents of the plugin request into ImageJ's plugins directory.
Scan rat femurs with a micro-CT machine following the standard scanning protocol.
Save the data in a format that can be imported into ImageJ, e.g., tiff format.
Import the data into ImageJ if multiple bone samples were scanned simultaneously.
Crop off other samples using ImageJ's image processing tools to separate each individual bone.
Save the resulting image in a format that can be imported into ImageJ later.
Open ImageJ software.
Under Plugins | BoMomics | Simulate Objects menu, click the Circle button.
Enter 200 as the diameter in the popup window.
Click OK to generate the simulated circle with a diameter of 200 pixels.
Save the generated circle in tiff format.
Open ImageJ software.
Under Plugins | BoMomics | Simulate Objects menu, click the Square button.
Enter 200 as the side length in the popup window.
Click OK to generate the simulated square with a side length of 200 pixels.
Save the generated square in tiff format.
Open ImageJ software.
Under the Plugins | BoMomics | Simulate Objects menu, click the Rectangle button.
Enter 200 as the width and 100 as the height in the popup window.
Click OK to generate the simulated rectangle with a width of 200 pixels and a height of 100 pixels.
Save the generated rectangle in tiff format.
Open ImageJ software.
Under the Plugins | BoMomics | Simulate Objects menu, click the Cube button.
Enter 30 as the side length in the popup window.
Click OK to generate the simulated cube.
Finally, click the Plugins | 3D | Volume Viewer to view the generated cube and save it in tiff format.
Open ImageJ software.
Under the Plugins | BoMomics | Simulate Objects menu, click the Cuboid button.
Enter 80 as the length, 40 as the width, and 30 as the height in the popup window.
Click OK to generate the simulated cuboid.
Finally, click the Plugins | 3D | Volume Viewer to view the generated cuboid and save it in tiff format.
Open ImageJ software.
Under the Plugins | BoMomics | Simulate Objects menu, click the Sphere button.
Enter 30 as the diameter in the popup window.
Click OK to generate the simulated sphere.
Finally, click the Plugins | 3D | Volume Viewer to view the generated sphere and save it in tiff format.
Open ImageJ software.
Under the Plugins | BoMomics | Simulate Objects menu, click the Cylinder button.
Enter 30 as the diameter and 100 as the height in the popup window.
Click OK to generate the simulated cylinder.
Click the Plugins | 3D | Volume Viewer to view the generated cylinder.
Save the cylinder in tiff format.
Open ImageJ software.
Open or import a scanned image.
Slide the bottom scrollbar to choose one slice.
Click the Image | Adjust | Threshold button.
In the popup Threshold window, adjust the minimum and maximum threshold values by manual inspection to ensure that bones are well separated from the background.
Record the minimal threshold value as the cortical bone threshold value.
Click the Plugins | BoMomics | Trab Param Profiling button.
Set Slice Index to the position of the representative slice.
Set cortical bone ("Cort Bone") threshold value.
Set range ("Range") value to 2,000.
Set step ("Step") value to 400.
Set Slice Index to 5 for the example dataset.
Open ImageJ software.
Open or import a scanned image.
Click the Plugins | BoMomics | Trab Segmentation button.
Set "Start" to 5.
Set "Outline Boundary" to 7.
Set "Trab. Bones" to 200.
Set "Noise Reduction Dia." to 7.
Set "Hole Filling Dia." to 6.
Set "Cortical Thickness Dia." to 12.
Click OK to perform trabecular segmentation.
Visually check the segmentation results in the Trab Segmentation Results window.
Save the extracted trabecular bones shown in the Segmented Trabecular Bones window in a tiff format.
Click the Plugins | BoMomics | Trab Analysis button.
Fill in appropriate analysis parameters: Set "Start" to 5.
Set "Outline Boundary" to 7.
Set "Trab. Bones" to 200.
Set "Noise Reduction Dia." to 7.
Set "Hole Filling Dia." to 6.
Set "Cortical Thickness Dia." to 12 and 25, respectively.
Select one or more choices in Results Reporting section for the parameters to be measured.
Check the checkboxes "2D" and "3D".
Click "OK" to perform trabecular analysis.
Select Plugins | BoMomics | Trab Analysis button.
Fill in appropriate analysis parameters as described previously.
Set "Noise Reduction Dia.", "Noise Reduction Dia.", "Hole Filling Dia.", and "Cortical Thickness Dia." to 0 for simulated objects.
Process 30 slices before and after the specified "Start" slice using the free version of the plugin.
Analyze only slices in the range specified by "Start" and "End" slices with the commercial version of the plugin.
Select "2D" and "3D" parameters to be measured in Results Reporting section.
Click OK to perform trabecular analysis for the simulated object.
Get calibration information from the scanned dataset according to the micro-CT vendor's instructions.
Open Microsoft Excel and open the reported results table.
Calculate calibrated bone volume (BVc) using the formula: BVc = BV × resolution^3 [μm³].
Calculate total volume (TVc) using the formula: TVc = TV × resolution^3 [μm³].
Calculate bone volume fraction (BV/TV) using the formula: BV/TV = BV ÷ TV.
Calculate bone mineral content (BMC) using the formula: BMC = (Intensity ÷ scaling × slope - BV × intercept) × resolution^3 × 10^-12 [mg HA].
Calculate bone mineral density (BMD) using the formula: BMD = BMC ÷ TVc × 10^12 [mg HA/cm³].
Create an XY (Scatter) plot for calibrated measures against slice layers using Microsoft Excel.
